Use case: stylized-concept. Input image is ONLY character identity and style REFERENCE, not an edit target. Generate a NEW production animation sprite sheet showing ONLY Row1 col1 silver armored cyan-visored assault soldier. Preserve exact design, colors, silhouette proportions from this one referenced character; do NOT include any other character. Asset type: transparent seven-action SIX-FRAME character animation atlas for ZERO PROTOCOL. Target canvas 1536 wide x 1792 high, EXACT SIX equal COLUMNS by SEVEN equal ROWS = 42 separately DRAWN sequential frames. Each row is one action, frames flow LEFT TO RIGHT in chronological order. No text, labels, numbers, borders or grid lines. Real transparent background. Crisp detailed chunky pixel art matching reference. Front three-quarter slightly overhead view, oriented right; same camera and body scale in every frame, character body centered at cell x50%, standing feet baseline y80%. Keep ALL limbs, effects and wreckage entirely inside central 70 percent of EACH cell, at least 15 percent transparent padding on all four sides. Never cross boundaries. Distinct actual limb articulation and different poses, not repeated static portraits or mere translations. Preserve same armor and facial identity through all 42 frames. Fixed registration for smooth playback; no ground, shadows, scenery or external particles. Row actions TOP TO BOTTOM:
ROW 1: idle: six subtly distinct breathing/reactor pulses, shoulders gently settle; loop
ROW 2: walk: six different alternating leg poses: left forward, passing, right plant, right forward, passing, left plant; swinging arms; seamless loop
ROW 3: shoot: raise arms, aim right, brace, recoil, ease recoil, return; no gun baked into sprite because game draws separate gun
ROW 4: melee: ready stance, draw back arm, windup torso, extend sword arm, follow through, recover; cyan energy blade
ROW 5: dash: crouch prepare, lean forward, fully launch, stretched forward stride, brake crouch, recover upright; no long external trails
ROW 6: hurt: impact recoil, shoulders back, bent knee, brace recovery, straighten, neutral; preserve cyan/amber identity
ROW 7: death: destabilize, stagger, buckle knees, fall forward, collapse, inert identifiable wreckage; nonempty last frame
All 42 cells must be occupied by exactly one complete frame. Limb motion visibly changes between every pair of columns; death progresses rather than loops. Do not enlarge dying wreckage or charge effects. Keep feet and body registration consistent, no clipping.
